stories.head: Blinkit Ambulance will now charge ₹2,500 for non-emergency trips
stories.dek: Emergency rides stay free. Routine trips like check-ups and hospital-to-home transfers will now be paid.
stat: charged for emergency rides — that doesn't change

sections.title: What happened
paras: Blinkit, the quick-commerce app owned by Eternal (formerly Zomato), runs its own ambulance service in a few cities. Until now, every ride was free.

On Thursday, Deepinder Goyal, Eternal's vice-chairman, announced that non-emergency trips will now cost ₹2,500 each. That covers things like routine check-ups, regular hospital visits and hospital-to-home transfers. The amount is collected after the trip and is roughly what private ambulances charge.
Emergency cases remain completely free.

sections.title: Why they did it
paras: According to Goyal, the service has done about 42,000 trips in two years, around 20,000 of them emergencies — and not one has been charged.

The problem: because rides were free, more and more people booked them for routine trips. Every routine booking takes an ambulance away from someone who might be having a heart attack or a stroke. The fee is meant to discourage that, so ambulances stay available for real emergencies.
The money collected goes to the Eternal Foundation, which runs the ambulances, to help expand the service.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: It's a rare case of a startup adding a price to make a free service work better, not to make money. Many people on social media backed the move, saying a free service only works if people don't misuse it.

stories.head: Deepinder Goyal hits back at doctors over his ‘Temple’ wearable
stories.dek: Doctors called the ₹85,000 brain-tracking gadget a scam. Goyal says the science will prove them wrong.
stat: of his own money put into Temple, Goyal says

sections.title: What is Temple?
paras: Temple is a small wearable that sits near the temple on the side of your head. It comes from Deepinder Goyal, the founder of Zomato, who stepped back from running Eternal to focus on it. It is priced at ₹85,000.
Goyal describes it as a fitness and wellness tracker — not a medical device.

sections.title: What the doctors are saying
paras: Several doctors on X have questioned the product. Their main argument: the device sits over the superficial temporal artery, which carries blood to the face and scalp — so it can't really be measuring blood flow to the brain, as its marketing suggests.
Some, including the well-known liver specialist who posts as ‘TheLiverDoc’, went further and called it a scam, saying there is no solid evidence behind its claims for such a high price.

sections.title: How Goyal responded
paras: Goyal rejected the scam claims on Thursday. He said that if the product were a scam, people would find out very quickly, and that its most important features haven't even been made public yet.
He says he has put about $20 million of his own money into the venture, and points to a 14-day, no-questions-asked return policy for anyone who isn't happy.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: It's a big test for one of India's best-known founders as he moves from food delivery into ‘deep tech’ health gadgets — a space where doctors and regulators expect hard scientific proof, not just good marketing.

stories.head: OpenAI could go public in 2027
stories.dek: The ChatGPT maker's president says the company could be ready for a stock market listing next year.
stat: growth in annualised revenue last quarter

sections.title: What happened
paras: Speaking at a Wall Street Journal tech conference, OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman was asked if the company could be ready for an IPO in 2027. His answer: “I think so. Yes.”
He added that OpenAI will list when the timing feels right, and that he feels very good about the business.

sections.title: The honest part
paras: Brockman admitted the first half of 2026 was “pretty rough” for OpenAI's business with companies. He also said OpenAI “wasn't even in the conversation” in AI coding agents — a space where rival Anthropic's Claude Code has been winning customers.

Things turned around in the third quarter: OpenAI's annualised revenue grew about 70% compared with the previous quarter, mainly because revenue from businesses doubled. Enterprise customers now bring in most of OpenAI's money.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: An OpenAI IPO would be one of the biggest stock market listings ever, and it would let ordinary investors own a piece of the company behind ChatGPT for the first time. It also signals that the AI race is shifting from consumer chatbots to selling AI to businesses.

stories.head: A viral video got a PVR juice counter shut in Bengaluru
stories.dek: A moviegoer alleged that used cups were being reused. Food safety officials inspected — and shut the counter.

sections.title: What happened
paras: A customer at the PVR INOX multiplex in Forum Mall, South Bengaluru, posted a video on Instagram showing a stack of used disposable cups. He alleged that staff were reusing cups that customers had already drunk from.
The video spread quickly. On its own, a video can't prove the allegation — but it was enough to get officials to act.

sections.title: What the authorities did
paras: Karnataka food safety officers inspected the outlet. The state said they found violations of food safety rules, issued a notice, and shut the juice counter. The exact violations haven't been made public yet.

sections.title: What the companies said
paras: Forum South Bengaluru apologised to the customer and said the PVR team was investigating the complaint and would take action.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: It shows how fast one customer's video can turn into government action against a big brand. For brands, the lesson is simple: in 2026, every customer is a reporter.

stories.credit: Syed Sajidul Islam / Wikimedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
stories.head: India set for a ₹1 lakh crore Dhanteras
stories.dek: Traders expect record shopping today — led by gold and silver, even though gold is about 20% costlier than last year.

sections.title: What's expected
paras: The Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) estimates that Indians will spend more than ₹1 lakh crore on Dhanteras today, the day traditionally seen as lucky for buying gold, silver, utensils and new things for the home.
Gold and silver alone are expected to bring in over ₹60,000 crore.

sections.title: The price problem
paras: 24-carat gold is around ₹1,41,840 per 10 grams — roughly 20% more than a year ago. Jewellers say many buyers are switching to lighter 14- and 18-carat pieces so they can still buy something without spending too much.

sections.title: The bigger picture
paras: CAIT expects total festive-season trade, from Navratri to Diwali, to cross ₹7 lakh crore — 15–18% more than last year. That's a strong sign that people are still spending, even with higher prices.

sections.title: What it means for you
paras: If you're buying gold today, compare making charges across jewellers and always check the BIS hallmark. Lighter 18-carat designs are a popular way to keep the tradition without stretching the budget.

stories.head: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football
stories.dek: After 23 years and a record 146 goals, the 41-year-old is done playing for Portugal — but he isn't leaving Al-Nassr.
stat: goals for Portugal, a national record

sections.title: What happened
paras: Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Thursday, in a video message, that he is retiring from international football. He called it “not an easy decision”.
He leaves after 234 matches for Portugal and 146 goals — the most in the team's history. He is also the only player to score at six different World Cups.

sections.title: Why now
paras: Portugal went out in the Round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup this summer, where Ronaldo scored three goals in five games. Reports say tensions with head coach Jorge Jesus had been building, and Ronaldo left the squad suddenly about five weeks ago.

sections.title: What's next
paras: He is not retiring from football completely. Ronaldo will keep playing for Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia, where his contract runs until June 2027. He is on 985 career goals — and chasing 1,000.

stories.credit: Architect of the Capitol / Wikimedia, Public domain
stories.head: Democrats win both houses of the US Congress
stories.dek: In Tuesday's midterm elections, Democrats took control of the House and the Senate — the first time in 20 years a Republican president has lost both.
stat: Senate seats won by Democrats so far (51 needed)

sections.title: What happened
paras: Americans voted on 3 November in the midterm elections, held halfway through a president's term. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 Senate seats were up for grabs, along with 36 governor races.

By Wednesday, the Associated Press tally showed Democrats with 228 House seats (218 is a majority) and 54 Senate seats (51 is a majority), with a few races still being counted. They flipped seats in states such as Texas, Kansas, Iowa, Michigan and South Carolina.

sections.title: Some firsts
paras: Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan and becomes the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor of a US state, in Georgia, and Deb Haaland the first Native American woman governor, in New Mexico.
President Trump told Fox News the Democrats "did a good job".

sections.title: Why it matters for India
paras: Congress writes US laws and approves spending, so the president now needs the other party for most new laws. Analysts quoted in Indian media expect it may limit how freely tariffs can be used, while Indian IT firms are watching for any change in the H-1B visa debate. Indian markets rose sharply at Thursday's open as investors reacted.

facts: Democrats: 228 House seats per AP, majority is 218
Last time a Republican president lost both houses: 2006

stories.head: Wall Street loses $2.5 trillion in a single day
stories.dek: The Nasdaq fell 5.5%, its worst day since April 2025, as AI and chip stocks crashed.
stat: chip stocks, worst day in ~6.5 years

sections.title: What happened
paras: US stocks had a brutal Thursday. The Nasdaq fell 5.52%, the S&P 500 fell 4.36% and the Dow dropped 1,833 points. About $2.5 trillion was wiped off the Nasdaq alone.
Chipmakers were hit hardest: Nvidia fell about 9%, while AMD and Micron fell around 17%.

sections.title: Why it happened
paras: After Democrats won both houses of Congress in the midterms, investors began to worry that new rules and local opposition could slow the building of AI data centers — the engine behind the AI boom. Weak results from Qualcomm added to the selling.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Indian markets opened lower on Friday too. Some analysts called it a knee-jerk reaction; others said the AI rally had become too speculative and needed to cool down.

stories.head: Tankers catch fire in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.dek: Iran says at least five tankers and a tugboat caught fire, several after hitting mines. Oil crossed $100 a barrel.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Iran's forces said several oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, some after hitting naval mines, and a tugboat sent to help also caught fire. A UK maritime agency separately reported a tanker hit by projectiles north of Qatar.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: About a fifth of the world's oil normally passes through this narrow strait. Traffic has been heavily restricted since the war involving Iran began in February, and attacks on ships are near record levels. Qatar is mediating talks, but no ceasefire is in place.

sections.title: What it means for you
paras: India imports most of its oil. If crude stays above $100, it can push up fuel prices and inflation.

stories.head: Iran lets Indian ships through the Strait of Hormuz
stories.dek: Indian vessels are exempt from Iran's shipping restrictions in the world's most important oil route — though they still pay a fee.

sections.title: What happened
paras: A senior Iranian lawmaker, Ahmad Hayat-Moghaddam of parliament's national security committee, said on Tuesday that ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar are exempt from Iran's restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz and can move freely.
Qatari ships pay no transit fee, he said, while Indian and Chinese vessels still have to pay charges. He linked India's exemption to keeping medicine imports into Iran flowing.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: A big share of the world's oil and gas passes through this narrow channel, and India buys most of its crude from abroad. Any delay there pushes up freight costs and, eventually, fuel prices. The exemption comes in the same week as fresh attacks on tankers in the strait, so it gives Indian shippers some relief — but the route is still far from normal.

facts: 4 countries exempted: India, China, Iraq, Qatar
Indian ships still pay transit charges

stories.head: Delhi's air turns "severe" before Diwali
stories.dek: The capital's average AQI crossed 450 this week, and stricter GRAP-II curbs are now in force across the NCR.
stat: Delhi's average AQI at 8 am on Tuesday

sections.title: What happened
paras: Delhi's air quality index hit 451 on Tuesday morning, according to Central Pollution Control Board data reported by ANI. Areas like Rohini, Punjabi Bagh and Bawana were in the 'severe' band, and most of the city was 'very poor'.
Later in the week, readings in parts of the NCR such as Ghaziabad, Noida and Faridabad were reported above 600.

sections.title: What changes
paras: The Commission for Air Quality Management has put Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) in force across the NCR. That means daily mechanical sweeping and water sprinkling on busy roads, tighter checks at construction sites and vehicle checks at the borders.

sections.title: What it means for you
paras: If you live in or are travelling to Delhi-NCR, an N95 mask, limiting early-morning outdoor exercise and keeping windows shut on the worst days all help. Diwali firecrackers usually make the following days worse.

facts: GRAP Stage II active across NCR

stories.head: Drone-delivery startup Zipline raises $1.5 billion
stories.dek: Its valuation has nearly tripled in about ten months, and Walmart is adding about 300 more drone-delivery locations.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Zipline, which delivers medicines and parcels by drone, raised $1.5 billion at a valuation of $21.5 billion. Paradigm, WCM Investment Management and Layer Global led the round, with Uber, Tiger Global, Fidelity, JPMorgan, ARK Invest and Salesforce Ventures also joining.
It also signed a multi-year deal with Walmart covering about 300 more delivery locations.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Earlier this year Zipline was valued at $7.6 billion. Investors are now betting that drone delivery moves from pilot projects to everyday shopping. Zipline started by flying blood and medicines in Africa, and has made nearly 3 million deliveries so far.

stories.head: Google plans a $17 billion AI data center in Wyoming
stories.dek: It will be Google's first in the state, powered largely by a giant fuel-cell plant.
stat: planned investment in one AI data center

sections.title: What happened
paras: Google announced plans for a $17 billion AI data center in Laramie County, Wyoming. It is being built with Tallgrass Energy, Black Hills Energy, American Electric Power and Related Digital.
Power will come mainly from a 702-megawatt fuel-cell project using Bloom Energy equipment, with carbon capture.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Big Tech is racing to build the computing power that AI needs. But the same week, voters in several US towns rejected new data centers over power bills and pollution — so companies are now trying to bring their own power instead of leaning on local grids. The $17 billion is a plan, not money already spent.

facts: Google's first data center in Wyoming
stories.alt: A Google data center (Council Bluffs, Iowa)

stories.head: Google, Meta and TikTok sue California over teen feeds law
stories.dek: The law limits autoplay and personalised feeds for users under 16. The companies say it breaks free-speech rules.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Google, Meta and TikTok filed a lawsuit to block California's Assembly Bill 1709. The law restricts features like autoplay and personalised recommendations for users under 16. Governor Gavin Newsom signed it in September, and it is due to start on 1 January 2027.
The companies argue it violates free speech. California's Attorney General says the state will defend it.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Endless scroll and autoplay are exactly what keep people on apps — and what critics say make them addictive for teenagers. Rules in big markets like California often end up shaping how apps work everywhere, so the case is being watched far beyond the US.

stories.head: OpenAI's new AI found 81 serious Firefox bugs
stories.dek: A cybersecurity model for approved researchers is finding and helping fix software holes at a scale humans could not.
stat: previously unknown high-severity Firefox bugs found

sections.title: What happened
paras: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber, a model only for authorised security researchers. Using it, researchers reported 81 previously unknown high-severity bugs in the Firefox browser and working exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities — with fixes released or in progress.
Access is limited at first through a programme called Daybreak Red.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: The same tools that help defenders find holes could help attackers too, which is why access is restricted. For everyday users, the takeaway is simple: keep your browser and phone updated, because many of these fixes arrive as routine updates.

stories.head: Airtel's profit jumps 24% as users pay more
stories.dek: Bharti Airtel's quarterly profit rose to ₹10,710 crore, helped by higher revenue per user.
stat: average revenue per user, up from ₹256

sections.title: The numbers
paras: Airtel's consolidated net profit for the September quarter rose 24% to ₹10,710 crore. Revenue grew 16.7% to about ₹60,878 crore, and India revenue rose 9.4%.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: The key number is ARPU — how much the average customer pays each month. It rose to ₹271 from ₹256 as more users moved to pricier plans. Airtel now has about 69 crore customers worldwide.

stories.credit: Piyush P Pujari / Wikimedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
stories.head: LIC's profit rises 20% to ₹12,076 crore
stories.dek: India's biggest insurer had a strong September quarter, though new first-year premiums dipped slightly.

sections.title: The numbers
paras: Life Insurance Corporation of India reported a standalone net profit of ₹12,076 crore for the quarter ended September, up 20%. Net premium income grew 16.2% to about ₹1.47 lakh crore.

sections.title: The catch
paras: First-year premium — money from brand-new policies — slipped slightly to ₹10,432 crore, and LIC flagged volatility in its market-linked (ULIP) products.

stories.head: Microsoft pulls back, AI cloud stocks tumble
stories.dek: Microsoft passed on a bigger deal with Nscale and is tightening oversight of its AI cloud partners. Their shares fell sharply.
stat: fall in Nebius and IREN shares

sections.title: What happened
paras: According to Bloomberg, Microsoft is keeping a closer eye on AI cloud providers Nscale, Nebius and IREN after construction delays and rising costs, and is leaning more on its own data centers. It declined an option to expand its Texas deal with Nscale; the existing contract stays.
Nebius and IREN shares fell more than 13%, and CoreWeave fell by double digits.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: These 'neoclouds' rent out AI computing power, and much of their value depends on big customers like Microsoft. Any sign that the giants are slowing down hits them hard — and it added to the wider sell-off in AI and chip stocks on Wall Street this week.

stories.head: Palantir's revenue nearly doubles to $2.31 billion
stories.dek: The data and AI software company had its first $2 billion quarter and raised its outlook for the year.
stat: quarterly revenue, nearly double last year

sections.title: What happened
paras: Palantir, which sells data and AI software to governments and companies, reported third-quarter revenue of $2.31 billion — almost twice what it made a year ago. It now expects about $8.5 billion in revenue for 2026.
Growth was led by US companies buying its AI platform.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Palantir has become one of the clearest examples of a company actually making money from AI, not just spending on it. But its shares are priced for a lot of future growth, so even strong results can be met with nervous trading — especially in a week when AI stocks were falling.

stories.head: India storm into the Asian Champions Trophy final
stories.dek: The defending champions beat South Korea 8-1 in the semi-final in Punjab to reach a record seventh final.

sections.title: What happened
paras: India's men's hockey team beat South Korea 8-1 in the semi-final of the Asian Champions Trophy, being played in Punjab, according to The Bridge. It is India's seventh final in the tournament — a record.
India had already beaten Korea 8-0 in the league stage and finished the group unbeaten.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: India are the defending champions and have been the strongest team in Asia this year. Winning again would build confidence ahead of a new-look squad for the FIH Pro League, which coach Craig Fulton has said he plans to field.

stories.head: TRAI proposes separate licences for satellite internet
stories.dek: The telecom regulator wants satellite players under a new set of rules — and not selling directly to customers.

sections.title: What happened
paras: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) on Thursday recommended a separate authorisation for satellite communication providers, along with a ‘network-as-a-service’ model.
Under the proposal, satellite companies would not be allowed to sell telecom services directly to consumers.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Satellite internet is the next big battleground in Indian telecom. These rules will shape how players like Starlink, Jio and Airtel's satellite ventures reach customers. The government still has to decide whether to accept TRAI's recommendations.

stories.head: 40 US towns vote NO to AI data centers
stories.dek: Voters rejected new data-center projects, angry about power bills and pollution.
stat: of voters in Trenton, Ohio backed a ban

sections.title: What happened
paras: In this week's US local elections, voters in nearly 40 towns rejected proposed data-center projects. In Trenton, Ohio, nearly 80% voted to ban large data centers that need more than 25 megawatts of power.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: AI runs on huge data centers that use massive amounts of electricity, water and land. Growing local pushback — plus fears that the new Congress could add rules — was one of the reasons tech stocks crashed on Thursday.

stories.head: AMD plans $11 billion in AI acquisitions
stories.dek: A filing shows the chipmaker wants to buy World Labs and inference-chip startup Taalas.

sections.title: What happened
paras: A quarterly filing showed AMD plans to buy World Labs Technologies for about $8.2 billion in stock and chip developer Taalas for about $2.9 billion in cash and stock, including up to $1.4 billion tied to future milestones. Both deals still need to close.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: AMD is Nvidia's main rival in AI chips. Buying startups is a fast way to add talent and technology — Taalas works on chips that run AI models cheaply after they are trained, which is where a lot of future demand is expected.

stories.head: Defence startup Shield AI buys Echodyne for $5.3 billion
stories.dek: The AI drone-pilot maker is buying a radar company and raising $2.5 billion at a $28.8 billion valuation.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Shield AI, which builds AI software that flies drones and aircraft, agreed to buy radar maker Echodyne for about $5.3 billion. To pay for it, Shield AI is raising $2.5 billion, including a $1 billion round at a $28.8 billion valuation, $1 billion from Blackstone-managed funds and $500 million of debt.
Echodyne sells radars in more than 40 countries. The deal is expected to close in early 2027.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Defence tech is one of the hottest areas for startup investors right now, driven by drones in modern warfare. Shield AI wants to own both the 'eyes' (radar) and the 'brain' (AI pilot) of autonomous systems.

stories.head: Grubhub owner Wonder files to go public
stories.dek: Marc Lore's food company — which also owns Blue Apron — has confidentially filed for a US IPO.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Wonder Group, founded by Marc Lore (who previously sold Jet.com to Walmart), confidentially submitted papers for a US stock market listing. The number of shares, price and valuation are not set yet.

Wonder owns food delivery app Grubhub, meal-kit brand Blue Apron and kitchen-robotics firm Spyce. It raised about $650 million in July at a reported $9 billion valuation, and plans drone deliveries in Texas with Zipline.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Wonder is trying to combine restaurants, delivery and kitchens under one roof — a similar bet to what Swiggy and Zomato make in India with their own kitchens and quick-commerce. Its IPO will be a test of whether investors like that model.

stories.head: India's services sector picks up speed in October
stories.dek: The HSBC India Services PMI rose to 55.8, showing faster growth in businesses like IT, banking, travel and retail.
stat: Services PMI in October (55.2 in September)

sections.title: What happened
paras: The HSBC India Services PMI — a monthly survey of purchasing managers — rose to 55.8 in October from 55.2 in September. Any reading above 50 means the sector is growing.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Services make up more than half of India's economy. A stronger reading during the festive month suggests demand is holding up even as some other numbers look softer. Other data this week was mixed: railway freight hit a record in October, while FMCG sales growth slowed.

stories.head: Deepti Sharma in the race for ICC Player of the Month
stories.dek: The all-rounder was shortlisted after a match-winning show against Zimbabwe.
stat: plus a five-wicket haul vs Zimbabwe

sections.title: What happened
paras: The ICC named Deepti Sharma on its shortlist for the Women's Player of the Month award for October. She scored an unbeaten 106 and took five wickets against Zimbabwe, as India swept the ODI series 3–0.

stories.head: What to watch this weekend on OTT
stories.dek: Dulquer Salmaan's I'm Game, Netflix's Dilwali Diwali and a new season of Black Doves lead this week's releases.

sections.title: The big ones
paras: I'm Game, starring Dulquer Salmaan, arrives on JioHotstar on 6 November in Malayalam, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada. Netflix has Dilwali Diwali (from the makers of Musafir Cafe) and the suspense series Black Doves, both from 5 November.
SonyLIV has Haiwaan and Meesaya Murukku 2 on 6 November, and ZEE5 has Last Man In Tower in Hindi.

sections.title: For the family
paras: Motu Patlu & The Mystery of Nagmani lands on JioHotstar on 8 November, and Minions & Monsters is already streaming there. Netflix also has the festive A Dog's Perfect Christmas.

stories.head: Joyalukkas sets aside ₹100 crore for charity
stories.dek: The jewellery brand will fund homes, girls' education, elderly care and medical help.
stat: for charity, announced on the founder's 70th birthday

sections.title: What happened
paras: Jewellery group Joyalukkas has set aside ₹100 crore to grow its charity work. The plan was announced in Kochi at the 70th birthday celebrations of its founder, Joy Alukkas.
The money will go to housing for families in need, education for girls, care for the elderly, medical help, women's empowerment and protecting the environment.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: The group says it has already built more than 550 homes across five southern states. It has promised a transparent system so the money reaches the people it is meant for.

stories.head: Tata Trusts gave ₹1,556 crore — and plans up to 50 hospitals
stories.dek: The Trusts want a network of not-for-profit hospitals where those who can pay help cover those who can't.
stat: given away by Tata Trusts in FY26

sections.title: What happened
paras: Tata Trusts gave away ₹1,556 crore in the year to March 2026 — on rural development, education, cancer care, healthcare, water and nutrition.
Chairman Noel Tata says the Trusts are now working towards a network of 40 to 50 not-for-profit general hospitals, where patients who can pay help fund care for those who cannot.

sections.title: The impact
paras: Its cancer care programme alone handled over 1 lakh outpatient visits, nearly 25,000 chemotherapy cycles and almost 30,000 radiotherapy patients last year.

stories.head: Gene therapy helps blind patients see objects again
stories.dek: In a new trial, people blinded by an inherited eye disease could detect and find everyday objects.
stat: patients became more sensitive to light

sections.title: What happened
paras: Scientists treated 10 people who had lost their sight to an inherited disease called retinitis pigmentosa. A gene therapy made surviving cells in the eye sensitive to light, and special goggles sent light patterns into the eye.
Seven of the ten became more sensitive to light, and several could find and recognise objects like a notebook or a small box. The results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: It's not normal vision yet — the researchers call the gains modest. But for people who could see almost nothing, being able to find objects again is a real step, and the treatment was judged safe in the trial.

stories.head: A short truce in Ukraine got nearly 800 people to safety
stories.dek: A six-day ceasefire in the town of Oleshky let aid in and people out. More peace talks are planned next week.

sections.title: What happened
paras: A local ceasefire in Oleshky, in southern Ukraine, held from 27 October to 1 November. It allowed humanitarian aid into the area and nearly 800 people were evacuated.
The truce was brokered with the help of US First Lady Melania Trump, who hosted representatives of both countries at the White House this week.

sections.title: What's next
paras: US officials say they will mediate talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November. A full peace deal is not agreed yet.

stories.head: Two teen brothers rescue a family from a flooded home
stories.dek: When emergency crews couldn't get through, they paddled in with a kayak and a paddleboard.

sections.title: What happened
paras: In Palm Bay, Florida, a mother and her young son were stuck on their kitchen counter with three dogs for over three hours as floodwater filled their home. Emergency crews couldn't reach them, so she asked for help on Facebook.
A woman who saw the post sent her two teenage sons. One borrowed a neighbour's kayak, the other took a paddleboard. They got the boy out first, then the mother and all three dogs.

sections.title: Why we love it
paras: Everyone made it to dry land — rescued by two kids who simply decided to go.

stories.head: 8 tiger cubs bring new hope to a Rajasthan sanctuary
stories.dek: It's the first successful tiger breeding recorded at Kailadevi in nearly 30 years.

sections.title: What happened
paras: A study by WWF-India and the Rajasthan Forest Department recorded eight tiger cubs and three adult tigers at Kailadevi Wildlife Sanctuary in Karauli over five years.
It's the first documented successful tiger breeding there in nearly three decades.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Kailadevi is next to Ranthambore. Tigers breeding here raises hopes of a second tiger population in the region, with forests linking to Madhya Pradesh's Kuno National Park.

stories.credit: Saffron, Leh / via The Better India
stories.head: Saffron blooms on barren land in Ladakh
stories.dek: A pilot farm in Leh flowered in under a month and gave 22 grams of saffron in four days.
stat: saffron picked in the first 4 days

sections.title: What happened
paras: Ladakh planted about 90,000 saffron corms on 4,000 square metres of restored land in Leh on 1 October. Flowers appeared in under 30 days — saffron usually takes about two months.
Nearly 22 grams of saffron were collected in the first four days.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Saffron is one of the world's most expensive spices, and around 90% of India's comes from Kashmir. If the pilot works at scale, it could give Ladakh's farmers and young people a valuable new income.

stories.head: Bengal's "Foodman" runs 20+ free study centres for children
stories.dek: A college professor gives children free meals and free coaching across West Bengal.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Chandrashekhar Kundu, a college professor from West Bengal known as the "Foodman", started by feeding about 180 children in three villages nearly ten years ago.
Today his initiative runs more than 20 free coaching centres, where children get help with schoolwork along with nutritious meals.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Hungry children find it hard to study. Pairing a meal with free tuition keeps kids in school — and it is happening right here in Bengal.

stories.credit: Kachra Café / via The Better India
stories.head: This Bhopal café swaps your trash for a meal
stories.dek: Bring plastic, paper or household waste — walk out with food. 45 tonnes recycled so far.

sections.title: What happened
paras: At Bhopal's Kachra Café, people bring plastic, paper and other household waste and trade it for food, drinks and everyday essentials. Each kilo of waste has a fixed value.
It was started by homemaker Anjita Sabhlok through her NGO, Mannat, with the Bhopal Municipal Corporation.

sections.title: The impact
paras: More than 45 tonnes of waste have been sent for recycling in eight months.

stories.head: IIT Bombay's free tool warns farmers of drought 4 weeks early
stories.dek: KrishiDrought uses satellites and AI to forecast dry soil for every district in India.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Researchers at IIT Bombay launched KrishiDrought, a free website that forecasts soil moisture up to four weeks ahead for every district in India, using satellite data, weather forecasts and deep learning.
A colour-coded map shows where soil is likely to be drier or wetter than normal.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: A few weeks' notice helps farmers plan irrigation and crops before a dry spell hits. It's free for anyone at KrishiDrought.in.

stories.head: Students fill a football field with food for families in need
stories.dek: A New Jersey high school collected more than 250,000 pounds of food in one drive.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Hundreds of students at Howell High School in New Jersey filled their football field with more than 250,000 pounds of food — the biggest drive in the organisers' history.
The food goes to about 30 food banks across the state.

sections.title: Why we love it
paras: It's a reminder of what a few hundred teenagers can do in a few days when they decide to help.
